stem: A particle moves along a semicircular path of radius 7 m from one end of the diameter to the other. The distance travelled and the magnitude of displacement are respectively (take π = 22/7):
explanation: Distance = length of the path = half the circumference = πr = (22/7) × 7 = 22 m. Displacement = straight-line distance between start and end points = the diameter = 2r = 14 m. Distance is path-dependent; displacement depends only on endpoints.
hint: One is the curved path length, the other is the straight line joining the two ends.
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line — distance vs displacement definitions

stem: Which of the following statements about average velocity is correct?
options: Average velocity = total displacement ÷ total time
Average velocity = total distance ÷ total time
Average velocity is always equal to average speed
Average velocity can never be zero for a moving particle
explanation: By definition, average velocity = total displacement / total time. Total distance / total time is average speed, a different quantity. If a particle returns to its starting point, displacement is zero, so average velocity is zero even though it moved.
hint: Velocity is tied to displacement, not distance. What happens on a round trip?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line — average velocity and average speed

stem: The position-time graph of a particle is a straight line with slope 3 m/s. The velocity of the particle is:
options: Cannot be determined from the graph
explanation: On an x–t graph, the slope at any point equals the instantaneous velocity: v = dx/dt. A straight line has constant slope everywhere, so velocity is constant at 3 m/s.
hint: What does the slope of an x–t graph represent?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line — position-time graphs

stem: A velocity-time graph forms a triangle with base 10 s and height 20 m/s, starting and ending at v = 0. The distance travelled is:
explanation: On a v–t graph, the area under the curve equals displacement (distance here, since velocity never goes negative). Area of triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 20 = 100 m.
hint: Area under a v–t graph gives you what?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line — velocity-time graphs

stem: A ball is dropped from rest from a height of 80 m. Taking g = 10 m/s² and neglecting air resistance, the time taken to reach the ground is:
explanation: For free fall from rest: h = ½gt² → t = √(2h/g) = √(2×80/10) = √16 = 4 s. Step-by-step: h = 80, g = 10, so 80 = 5t², t² = 16, t = 4 s (positive root).
hint: Use h = ½gt² and solve for t.
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line — motion under gravity; H.C. Verma Concepts of Physics Vol.1 Ch.3

stem: A projectile is launched with speed 20 m/s at 45° to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², its horizontal range is:
explanation: Range R = u²sin2θ/g. At θ = 45°, sin2θ = sin90° = 1, so R = u²/g = 400/10 = 40 m. Note 45° gives maximum range for a given speed on level ground.
hint: What is sin(2θ) when θ = 45°? Then use R = u²sin2θ/g.
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Plane — projectile motion; H.C. Verma Concepts of Physics Vol.1 Ch.4

stem: Car A moves at 60 km/h and car B moves at 40 km/h in the same direction on a straight highway. The velocity of A as observed by the driver of B is:
options: 20 km/h in the direction of motion
100 km/h in the direction of motion
20 km/h opposite to the direction of motion
explanation: Relative velocity v_AB = v_A − v_B = 60 − 40 = 20 km/h. Since A is faster in the same direction, B's driver sees A pulling ahead at 20 km/h in the direction of motion.
hint: Relative velocity = velocity of A minus velocity of B. Mind the signs.
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Plane — relative velocity

stem: The dimensional formula of acceleration is:
explanation: Acceleration = change in velocity / time. Velocity has dimensions [LT⁻¹]; dividing by time [T] gives [LT⁻¹]/[T] = [LT⁻²].
hint: Acceleration is (velocity)/(time). What are the dimensions of velocity?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Units and Measurements — dimensions of physical quantities

stem: The speedometer of a car measures:
explanation: A speedometer shows the speed at the instant you look at it — the magnitude of the instantaneous velocity. Average quantities require total distance/displacement over a time interval, which a speedometer does not compute.
hint: Does the needle show your trip average or your speed right now?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line — instantaneous velocity

stem: For a particle in uniform circular motion, which statement is correct?
options: Velocity is tangential and acceleration is directed towards the centre
Both velocity and acceleration are tangential
Velocity is radial and acceleration is tangential
Both velocity and acceleration are zero
explanation: In uniform circular motion speed is constant but direction changes continuously, so velocity is always tangential. The change in direction requires a centripetal acceleration directed towards the centre, of magnitude v²/r.
hint: Speed is constant — so what must be changing? What causes that change?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Plane — uniform circular motion

stem: A particle starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration 4 m/s². Its velocity after 3 s is:
explanation: Use v = u + at with u = 0. Step-by-step: v = 0 + 4 × 3 = 12 m/s.
hint: Which SUVAT equation connects u, a, t and v?
source: H.C. Verma Concepts of Physics Vol.1 Ch.3 — equations of uniformly accelerated motion

stem: A particle starts with velocity 10 m/s and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s². The distance covered in 5 s is:
explanation: Use s = ut + ½at². Step-by-step: s = 10×5 + ½×2×25 = 50 + 25 = 75 m.
hint: s = ut + ½at². Plug in the numbers carefully.
source: H.C. Verma Concepts of Physics Vol.1 Ch.3 — equations of uniformly accelerated motion

stem: A stone is dropped from rest. Taking g = 10 m/s², its velocity after falling 20 m is:
explanation: Use v² = u² + 2as with u = 0, a = g = 10, s = 20. Step-by-step: v² = 0 + 2×10×20 = 400 → v = 20 m/s.
hint: No time is given — which equation avoids t?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line — motion under gravity

stem: A ball is thrown vertically upward with speed 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s², the maximum height reached is:
explanation: At maximum height v = 0. Use v² = u² − 2gH. Step-by-step: 0 = 400 − 20H → H = 400/20 = 20 m. Equivalently H = u²/2g.
hint: At the top, velocity is momentarily zero. Use v² = u² + 2as with a = −g.
source: H.C. Verma Concepts of Physics Vol.1 Ch.3 — vertical motion under gravity

stem: The position-time graph of a particle curves upward (slope increasing with time). This means the particle is:
explanation: Slope of the x–t graph = velocity. If the slope keeps increasing, velocity is increasing with time — the particle is speeding up (positive acceleration).
hint: Slope of x–t = velocity. What does an increasing slope mean?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line — interpreting position-time graphs

stem: The velocity-time graph of a particle is a horizontal straight line. The acceleration of the particle is:
explanation: Slope of the v–t graph = acceleration. A horizontal line has zero slope, so acceleration is zero — the particle moves with uniform (constant) velocity.
hint: Slope of v–t = acceleration. What is the slope of a horizontal line?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line — velocity-time graphs

stem: A person walks 3 m east and then 4 m west along a straight road. The total distance walked and the magnitude of displacement are:
explanation: Distance adds up regardless of direction: 3 + 4 = 7 m. Displacement = final position − initial position = 3 − 4 = −1 m, i.e. 1 m to the west. Magnitude = 1 m.
hint: Distance accumulates; displacement is just start-to-finish.
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line — distance and displacement

stem: A scooter covers 60 km in 2 hours without changing direction. Its average speed is:
explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time = 60/2 = 30 km/h. (Since direction never changed, average velocity has the same magnitude.)
hint: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line — average speed

stem: At the highest point of its trajectory, a projectile has:
options: Zero vertical velocity but non-zero horizontal velocity
Zero horizontal velocity but non-zero vertical velocity
explanation: The vertical component decreases to zero at the top (it momentarily stops rising), but the horizontal component u·cosθ never changes (no horizontal force, neglecting air resistance). So speed at the top = u·cosθ, the minimum speed of the flight.
hint: Which component of velocity is affected by gravity?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Plane — projectile motion

stem: A projectile is launched at 30° with speed 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s², the time taken to reach the highest point is:
explanation: Time to top = u·sinθ / g (half the total time of flight). Step-by-step: u·sinθ = 20 × 0.5 = 10 m/s; t = 10/10 = 1 s.
hint: Time to the top is half the total flight time: t = u·sinθ/g.
source: H.C. Verma Concepts of Physics Vol.1 Ch.4 — projectile motion

stem: Two trains move towards each other on parallel tracks at 40 km/h and 60 km/h. The speed of one train as seen from the other is:
explanation: For motion in opposite directions, relative speed adds up. Step-by-step: v_rel = 40 + 60 = 100 km/h (take one direction positive, the other negative, then subtract).
hint: Opposite directions: do the speeds add or subtract?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Plane — relative velocity

stem: A particle moves in a circle of radius 2 m with a time period of 4 s. Its speed is approximately:
explanation: Speed = circumference / period = 2πr/T. Step-by-step: 2 × 3.14 × 2 / 4 = 12.56/4 = 3.14 m/s.
hint: In one period the particle covers one full circumference, 2πr.
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Plane — uniform circular motion

stem: From a velocity-time graph, a particle's velocity changes from 5 m/s to 25 m/s in 4 s with uniform acceleration. The acceleration is:
explanation: Acceleration = slope of v–t graph = Δv/Δt. Step-by-step: (25 − 5)/4 = 20/4 = 5 m/s².
hint: Acceleration is the slope: change in velocity divided by time.
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line — acceleration from v–t graph

stem: Which equation of motion does NOT involve displacement?
explanation: v = u + at links only velocity, initial velocity, acceleration and time — displacement s appears in the other three equations.
hint: Look for the equation with no 's' in it.
source: H.C. Verma Concepts of Physics Vol.1 Ch.3 — kinematic equations

stem: The SI unit of acceleration is:
explanation: Acceleration = velocity/time = (m/s)/s = m/s². The newton (N) is the unit of force, not acceleration.
hint: Acceleration is velocity divided by time — combine their units.
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Units and Measurements — SI units

stem: A ball thrown vertically upward is momentarily at rest at its highest point. At that instant, its acceleration is:
explanation: Zero velocity does not mean zero acceleration. Gravity acts throughout the flight, so at the top the ball still accelerates downward at g ≈ 10 m/s² — that is exactly why its velocity starts increasing downward right after.
hint: Does gravity switch off at the top of the flight?
source: H.C. Verma Concepts of Physics Vol.1 Ch.3 — velocity vs acceleration

stem: If the acceleration of a particle is zero throughout its motion, then:
explanation: Zero acceleration means velocity does not change — it stays constant in both magnitude and direction (uniform motion). Constant velocity need not be zero; a car cruising at steady 60 km/h has zero acceleration.
hint: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. If the rate is zero…?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line — uniform motion

stem: Which of the following is an example of motion in a plane (two dimensions)?
options: A car moving on a straight road
A train on a straight track
explanation: A projectile moves simultaneously horizontally and vertically — its position needs two coordinates (x, y), so it is motion in a plane. The others are confined to a straight line (one dimension).
hint: How many coordinates do you need to locate the object at any instant?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Plane — introduction

stem: A particle moves with constant speed 10 m/s along a circular path. Which quantity is changing with time?
explanation: Speed (magnitude) is constant at 10 m/s, but the direction of motion keeps changing along the circle. Since velocity includes direction, velocity is changing — that is why there is a centripetal acceleration even at constant speed.
hint: Velocity is a vector. What happens to its direction on a circle?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Plane — uniform circular motion

stem: The area under an acceleration-time graph between t = 0 and t = T gives:
explanation: Since a = dv/dt, integrating gives Δv = ∫a dt — the area under the a–t graph equals the change in velocity over that interval. (Similarly: area under v–t = displacement, slope of x–t = velocity, slope of v–t = acceleration.)
hint: a = dv/dt. What do you get when you 'accumulate' a over time?
source: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line — acceleration-time graphs
